definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C) generated by X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for all integers r≥0; its action on V is the given representation extended to the enveloping algebra.

definitions.type: subring of Q, embedded in C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}, with operations inherited from Q. A unit of R means an element having a multiplicative inverse in R.
M_R is the R-span of M in V, namely all finite sums of r_j m_j with r_j∈R and m_j∈M. The canonical map R⊗_Z M→M_R sends r⊗m to rm; its injectivity is to be proved, not assumed.
For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex-linear map with E_ij(e_k)=δ_jk e_i for all k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise. This construction requires that e be a complex basis of V.
For every natural d, factorial(d)=d!=∏_{t=1}^d t; the product for d=0 is 1.
For natural a,r, binom(a,r) is the number of r-element subsets of {1,...,a}; in particular it is zero for r>a and binom(a,0)=1.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0≤λ<p.

M is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup of V admitting an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. The choice of M is arbitrary, not restricted to the minimal lattice.

e=(e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Also y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. On the basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

inputs.statement: For a semiring A satisfying the strong rank condition, an additive commutative monoid T with an A-module structure, a finite index type C, and an A-basis d of T indexed by C, finrank_A(T)=card(C). Here finrank is the natural-valued module rank, and the strong rank condition says an injective A-linear map A^u→A^v forces u≤v for finite natural u,v.

output.statement: The map R⊗_Z M→M_R, a_R⊗m↦a_R m, is an R-linear isomorphism, M_R has an R-basis indexed by I, and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r for r≥0 preserves M_R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λ X_λ)Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. More explicitly Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, and E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}.

locals.declaration: Choose a finite index set A for an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V, as supplied by admissibility H004; finite dimensionality is supplied by the basis N001.
Choose the corresponding integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V.
Define Qop=Y_λ X_λ; this is the projector denoted P in the supplied proof, renamed to avoid collision with the target ID.

argument.text: By H004 choose an integer basis m indexed by A which is also a complex basis. It is finite because V has the finite basis N001. M002 over C gives card(A)=dim_C V=card(I)=n. Reindexing by a bijection therefore permits an I-indexed basis. M001, with scalar extension Z→R, gives an R-basis (1⊗m_a) of R⊗_Z M. The multiplication map r⊗m↦rm sends this basis to the same vectors m_a in V. Their complex independence implies R-independence, and their R-span is M_R by definition. Thus this map is injective and onto M_R, and the images form an R-basis with n elements, reindexed by I.

produces.statement: The canonical map R⊗_Z M→M_R is an R-linear isomorphism, M_R has a basis indexed by I, and its complex span is V.

argument.text: Every X_r and Y_r preserves M by H004 and D006. By complex linearity, it preserves the R-span M_R. Also M_R contains the basis vectors m_a, so its complex span is V, as recorded in F001. These statements do not restrict M to the minimal lattice.

produces.statement: For every natural r, X_r(M_R)⊆M_R and Y_r(M_R)⊆M_R.

argument.text: Define Qop=Y_λ X_λ. Test N001 on every e_k: X_λ kills k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0, while Y_λ e_0=e_λ; hence Qop=E_{λλ}. Likewise X_{λ-i}Qop=E_{iλ}, since X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i. Finally Qop Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}: an input e_k with k<j lands below e_λ and is killed by Qop; one with k>j passes the end of the y-string and vanishes; at k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). These identities hold for all i,j∈I, including λ=0.

produces.statement: Qop=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}Qop=E_{iλ}, and Qop Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj} for every i,j∈I.

argument.text: For every j∈I, H001 and M007 show p divides none of λ!, j!, (λ-j)!. These integers therefore have inverses in R by its denominator definition. The identity binom(λ,j)=λ!/(j!(λ-j)!) makes this binomial a unit in R. Composing F003 gives X_{λ-i}Qop Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_ij, whence E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. F002 and closure of the R-module M_R under R-scalars prove preservation by every E_ij. F001 supplies the basis and scalar-extension assertions. No reduced h-eigenvalue argument has been used.
